# CUDA-Q parity matrix

This scoreboard is generated from `contracts/cudaq-parity-matrix.toml`. It compares the CUDA-Q capability baseline against FlagQuantum. FlagQuantum maturity levels, owners, limitations, and evidence paths are read from `capability-maturity.toml` and are not restated here; a row whose registry column reads `none` has no registered maturity entry.

- CUDA-Q baseline versions: 0.15.1, 0.16.0.post1
- Pinned component: CUDA-Q core
- Baseline component: cudaq-qec, also shipped as libs/qec inside NVIDIA/cudaqx
- Component release line: 0.1.0, 0.2.0, 0.2.1, 0.3.0, 0.4.0, 0.4.0.post1, 0.5.0, 0.5.0.post1, 0.6.0, 0.7.0, 0.8.0
- Component version the `quantum_error_correction` rows were read at: 0.8.0
- Component release index: https://pypi.org/pypi/cudaq-qec/json

The top-level cudaq_versions pin describes CUDA-Q core, which is the product both the export contract and this matrix describe. The QEC component ships on its own release line, so a quantum_error_correction row is only as strong as the component version it was read at, and this table records that version separately rather than implying that the pin reaches it. The tool fails closed in both directions: a pin that overlaps the component release line needs a mapping entry, and a mapping entry across two lines that do not overlap is refused as a correspondence nothing supports.

Provenance limit: No cudaq-qec release maps to either pinned CUDA-Q version: the component's release line runs from 0.1.0 to 0.8.0 while the pin is 0.15.1 and 0.16.0.post1, and the two lines are disjoint. Every quantum_error_correction row therefore records the component surface as it stands at 0.8.0. That the same surface exists at the pinned CUDA-Q baseline is not established by this contract, so a QEC row must not be read as a statement about CUDA-Q 0.15.1 or 0.16.0.post1, and a row that needs to be is a new capture rather than a new reading.
- Baseline survey: `docs/development/CUDAQ_PARITY_BASELINE.md`
- Capture method: documented_capability_survey_with_probes
- Scope: CUDA-Q capabilities observable from the public Python API, the documented backend roster, and the shipped repository tree of the pinned versions.

Baseline probes:

A probe is a runnable repository script whose JSON payload can be landed as evidence. `runnable` means the probe starts and emits its schema. `measured` means a payload from a named machine is landed under benchmarks/results with the source revision, container image, environment, and methodology recorded next to it, and that benchmarks/audit_results.py accepts it. Every probe must declare a versioned schema identifier and a source identity.

| Probe | Status | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `benchmarks/cudaq_gradient_capability_probe.py` | measured | Which gradient strategies the installed CUDA-Q exposes through cudaq.gradients, by runtime public-symbol inspection. |
| `benchmarks/cudaq_backend_compare.py` | measured | Wall-clock and precision comparison of one FlagQuantum JAX kernel against one CUDA-Q target on a matched circuit, observable, dtype, gradient method, warmup, and iteration count. |

First capture, `benchmarks/cudaq_gradient_capability_probe.py`: CUDA-Q 0.16.0.post1 exported ParameterShift, CentralDifference, ForwardDifference, and gradient, and exposed no adjoint, reverse, or backprop symbol. On 2026-09-30 the same survey ran three times on each of jp-a800-172 and jp-a800-171, against cuda-quantum-cu12 and cuda-quantum-cu13 respectively, and returned a byte-identical capability record on both hosts, so the statement is a property of the release rather than of one installed wheel.

Landed payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/cudaq_gradient_capability_a800_20260930.json`

Reading of that payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/CUDAQ_BACKEND_COMPARE_A800_20260930.md`

First capture, `benchmarks/cudaq_backend_compare.py`: On 2026-09-30 on jp-a800-172 and jp-a800-171, one A800-SXM4-80GB per host and CUDA-Q 0.16.0.post1 on both, the FlagQuantum JAX kernel matched CUDA-Q numerically on every configuration measured on both hosts: the largest loss deviation was 1.2e-05 and the largest gradient deviation 1.8e-05 against a 1e-4 tolerance, and every FlagQuantum timing agreed across hosts to within 10 percent. CUDA-Q's nvidia target was faster for forward-only execution at every width, widening from 1.4x at 8 wires to 89x at 22 wires, and that conclusion was insensitive to the warmup count. The FlagQuantum fused value-and-gradient program was faster per call, but its 18-wire ratio moved monotonically from 13.6x to 16.3x between one and five warmups, so an earlier 7.9x reading of the same configuration is withdrawn as under-warmed rather than reproduced.

Landed payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/cudaq_backend_compare_a800_20260930.json`

Reading of that payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/CUDAQ_BACKEND_COMPARE_A800_20260930.md`

Baseline component ownership:

A domain `cudaq_surface` list is an inventory of the surface a QEC user meets, and an inventory is not an attribution: three components of one product appear in those lists. Most items belong to cudaq-qec, which is the component this domain compares against. The entries below are the items whose owner is a different component, or whose owner is worth stating, and each records what that ownership means for the row it feeds. An attributed item must appear verbatim in exactly one domain surface list, so the table cannot drift from the inventory it explains, and an item owned by another component must state its consequence, so a reader cannot follow the inventory to the wrong owner. Only contested or non-obvious items are listed; the absence of an entry is not a claim about ownership.

| CUDA-Q surface item | Owning component |
| --- | --- |
| detector, detectors, and logical_observable annotations in a kernel | `cudaq-core` |
| dem, dem_from_kernel, and DEMResult | `cudaq-core` |
| extract_syndrome | `cudaq-logical-preview` |
| the logical.* preview namespace | `cudaq-logical-preview` |
| for-stim-users migration | `cudaq-logical-preview` |
| Stim integration | `cudaq-qec` |

- `cudaq-core`, detector, detectors, and logical_observable annotations in a kernel: These annotations are CUDA-Q core kernel syntax rather than a cudaq-qec API, and core's dem_from_kernel is what reads them back. The row the annotations feed therefore belongs to the core capability set, and whether FlagQuantum grows a kernel annotation surface is a language-level decision rather than a QEC library one.
- `cudaq-core`, dem, dem_from_kernel, and DEMResult: One surface item, two owners, so it must be read as two. dem_from_kernel and DEMResult are CUDA-Q core: both are documented on the core Python API page and neither appears in the cudaq-qec Python API, which exposes no dem_from_kernel and no DEMResult anchor at all. cudaq-qec's own construction entries are dem_from_stim_text, dem_from_memory_circuit with its x_ and z_ variants, and dem_from_css_matrices, and cudaq-qec consumes the core record rather than declaring it. Construction is only a cudaq-qec row when it is read against those entries; the core record is a dependency of the row, not its baseline.
- `cudaq-logical-preview`, extract_syndrome: extract_syndrome belongs to the CUDA-Q Logical preview layer, not to cudaq-qec: it appears in that layer's Stim emission material as the encoded operation a fabric call expands into, it is absent from the cudaq-qec Python API, and it is absent from the core Python API page. cudaq-qec's own extraction route is sample_memory_circuit with its x_ and z_ variants, feeding decoder_context_from_memory_circuit. Aligning to the preview layer would not deliver the detector error model this domain is built around, because that layer states of itself that it does not simulate, sample, or decode and emits no detector error models. Either the surface item is misattributed here, or the preview layer is a second target with a different deliverable.
- `cudaq-logical-preview`, the logical.* preview namespace: The namespace is preview-layer scope, not a cudaq-qec surface. The semantic core inside it -- lattice surgery, product rotation, distillation -- is what the qec_logical_operations row tracks through the Qualtran adaptation, while the namespace's patch, gadget, protocol, and program records are that layer's own shape and not a FlagQuantum target.
- `cudaq-logical-preview`, for-stim-users migration: cudaq-qec ships no for-Stim-users page. The only page with that title in the CUDA-Q documentation belongs to the logical preview layer, and it states there that the layer does not simulate, sample, or decode, emits no detector annotations and no detector error models, and that those studies belong to the Stim ecosystem. It is therefore not a cudaq-qec counterpart, and the qec_stim_user_migration document has to be written against cudaq-qec's own surface -- dem_from_stim_text, dem_sampling, the decoder framework, and decoding from Stim DEM text -- rather than translated from that page.
- `cudaq-qec`, Stim integration: Stim appears on both sides of the product split, so the item needs its cudaq-qec half named. Reading Stim detector error model text, and decoding from Stim DEM text, are cudaq-qec's: dem_from_stim_text and the decoder framework's Stim entry point are in the cudaq-qec Python API. Emitting Stim from a verified gadget is the preview layer's and is not a cudaq-qec capability. A row that reads only the second half would compare this repository against a component that does not decode.

- Limitation: A capability absent from this matrix is not evidence that CUDA-Q lacks it; it is evidence that the survey did not record it.
- Limitation: The pinned versions are the ones the repository already targets in contracts/cudaq-export-contract.toml. A CUDA-Q release outside that range requires a new capture.
- Limitation: No row in this file is a performance comparison. Measured numbers belong in benchmarks/results and require an audited payload.
- Limitation: A `runnable` probe is not a recorded measurement. CUDA-Q is not installable from the pinned public index as a binary wheel: the PyPI `cudaq` release is an sdist whose build hook resolves a platform binary distribution at install time. No CI lane in this repository runs either probe, so a payload is only ever captured by hand on a machine that reaches a working CUDA-Q index.
- Limitation: A landed payload describes only the machines, revision, and workload it names. It is not scalability evidence and it does not generalise to other widths, observables, targets, or CUDA-Q releases.
- Limitation: A gradient-path ratio is not a simulation-throughput ratio. The two sides do not execute the same schedule, so a value-and-gradient comparison measures host call structure as well as arithmetic.
- Limitation: The recorded protocol has not been shown to reach steady state for the gradient configurations. A gradient ratio is only meaningful together with the warmup count that produced it, and a settled protocol needs a per-configuration convergence check rather than a fixed warmup count.

No row in this document is a performance comparison or a scalability claim.

### Dependency class of every open gap

The replacement battlefield is the set of capabilities where the CUDA-Q implementation sits on an NVIDIA-proprietary component. Each such capability is a gap FlagQuantum must close with its own kernel or with a FlagOS-family component, not by depending on the NVIDIA original.

| Dependency class | Open gaps | Closed | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A_nvidia_proprietary | 8 | 1 | 9 |
| B_open_neutral | 16 | 0 | 16 |
| C_flagos_replacement | 2 | 1 | 3 |
| none | 60 | 7 | 67 |

### Next work, by priority

**now** (33 open)

- `python_ast_kernel` (language_and_programming_model): FlagQuantum builds circuits through an explicit builder API. There is no AST layer, so a user cannot write a Python function body as a kernel.
- `kernel_first_class_functions` (language_and_programming_model): The public CircuitIR schema 1.0 has no function or call construct. The internal levels designed in MULTI_LEVEL_IR_ARCHITECTURE.md 5.2 do, and are the planned home.
- `classical_control_flow` (language_and_programming_model): CircuitIR 1.0 expresses a straight-line instruction list. Classical values with def-use, blocks, branches, and bounded loops are designed but not implemented.
- `control_adjoint_modifiers` (language_and_programming_model): Only the named gates ccx and cswap provide multi-controlled forms, and no adjoint modifier exists. A unitary passed through Circuit.any is not a modifier.
- `type_system_qubit_register_view` (language_and_programming_model): CircuitIR 1.0 addresses wires by integer index and has no type system. The designed QuantumIR type system and its reference-versus-value linearity rules are not implemented.
- `dynamic_kernel_measurement_feedback` (language_and_programming_model): FlagQuantum implements this through runtime/dynamic with a candidate-stable public namespace. The registered level is below production, and the surface is narrower than the CUDA-Q baseline.
- `custom_operation_registration` (language_and_programming_model): Circuit.any accepts a raw unitary but there is no operation registry, no schema, and no backend degradation contract for a user-defined operation.
- `pass_manager_and_pass_plugins` (compiler_and_ir): The pass and analysis contracts and the CompilerPassExtension protocol are designed, and the ecosystem SDK exposes the extension kind, but no pass manager consumes the protocol and compilation paths remain fixed pipelines.
- `topology_aware_routing` (compiler_and_ir): Routing, topology legalization, and directional topology modules exist as a skeleton, but there is no published-quality router comparable to a SABRE-class algorithm.
- `qir_code_generation` (compiler_and_ir): FlagQuantum emits OpenQASM and QCIS text only. QIR is an open specification with no NVIDIA dependency, so this is the highest-value compiler gap after the internal levels.
- `compiler_plugin_ecosystem` (compiler_and_ir): The extension protocol and lifecycle exist, but no discovery path reaches compilation, so an out-of-tree pass cannot run.
- `backend_multi_gpu_statevector` (simulation_backends): Sharded statevector training exists at development_evidence level with one measured 32-qubit complex128 forward pass on one eight-accelerator node. Production capacity expansion is not established.
- `backend_tensor_network_exact` (simulation_backends): A self-built PyTorch tensor-network path exists without a cuTensorNet-class contraction planner, so the exact regime is narrower than the CUDA-Q baseline.
- `backend_density_matrix` (simulation_backends): An engine exists in the simulation domain, but it has no capability-maturity.toml entry, so it carries no recorded owner, limitation set, or hardware evidence.
- `backend_stim_stabilizer` (simulation_backends): Both halves of the row now exist in a narrower form. The representation half is closed: a Stim-backed Clifford sampling engine samples a thousand-wire GHZ chain, so the wire counts a dense amplitude store cannot hold are reachable, and Stim is Apache-2.0 licensed and independent of every NVIDIA component, which is why this was integration rather than research. The execution half landed as an execution mode: `plan` and `run` reach the engine through `state_mode='stabilizer'` and report a plan, a result, and execution evidence, which `tests/integration/test_stabilizer_execution_mode.py` pins. What remains is narrower than the baseline in three ways: no expectation values over the representation, no noise, and no detector error model connected to it.
- `backend_dynamics` (simulation_backends): FlagQuantum has a real Lindblad engine with RK4 integration, validation codes, and evidence fields, so this capability is not missing. Three walls separate it from the baseline: CPU-only hard rejection, a dense four-to-the-n Hamiltonian with a fixed step, and a static Hamiltonian. Batching and gradients are rejected.
- `kraus_channel_algebra` (noise_and_error_models): A general Kraus constructor exists and is validated. `KrausChannel` accepts an arbitrary operator list, refuses a set that is not trace-preserving (completeness compared at `atol = rtol = 1e-6`) and a dimension that is not a positive power of two, serializes through the `flagquantum.kraus_channel.v1` schema, and reaches simulation through `NoiseModel.add` and `Circuit.noisy_density_matrix`. What is absent is the operator type the CUDA-Q surface builds a channel from: no matrix-valued operator participates in operator algebra, which is the gap `matrix_and_custom_operator` already records.
- `detector_error_model` (noise_and_error_models): Both directions of the stim text interchange work. `from_memory_circuit` builds a model exactly for Pauli noise over the reference Clifford gate set; `to_stim_text` emits text stim 1.16.0 parses; `from_stim_text` reads everything stim wrote in a 240-model developer-time sweep except a `repeat` block, and `str(model.flattened())` is a complete route around that one refusal; both readings of a `^` separator are offered under upstream's own `use_decomp_suggestions` flag name, and the default is the one stim itself means, measured against stim's own sampler rather than asserted. The row stays partial because conversion is narrower than the baseline at the input end: `from_memory_circuit` accepts one circuit record and one noise record, so an arbitrary circuit carrying detector and observable annotations has no route to a model, and a non-Pauli channel is refused rather than decomposed. `flagquantum/qec/IMPLEMENTATION.md` records the sweeps and the arithmetic.
- `spin_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Pauli observables exist. Operator arithmetics for products, sums, scalars, exponentials, commutators, and anticommutators are absent.
- `fermion_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Absent. It is the precondition for a chemistry workflow and for exact fermionic observable construction.
- `super_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Absent. The Lindblad engine applies a dense Hamiltonian and a collapse-operator list directly, without a vectorized superoperator form, which is one of the three walls limiting its scale.
- `chemistry_domain_library` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Absent, and it is the first entry point for most chemistry users. The underlying integrals come from PySCF, which is open and vendor-neutral.
- `execution_entry_points` (algorithm_layer): Run, counts, expectation, compile, and plan exist. evolve and translate have no equivalent, and draw exists in a narrower form.
- `error_mitigation` (algorithm_layer): Zero-noise extrapolation only. An observable is measured at several error strengths by scaling the one error-probability parameter each noise channel declares, and the curve is continued to zero by polynomial least squares or Richardson extrapolation, which reports the residual it left and the variance amplification of its weights. The channel families whose parameters are not error probabilities are refused by name, and a model that declares a readout rule is refused rather than measured without it, because the estimate is Tr(O rho) and classical readout confusion is applied after measurement. Probabilistic error cancellation and Clifford data regression are absent, and so is readout-error mitigation.
- `variational_algorithms` (algorithm_layer): VQE-class and several algorithm primitives exist as separate registered capabilities rather than a solver family, so the surface shape differs from the baseline.
- `qec_code_library` (quantum_error_correction): The repetition code, the rotated surface code and the Steane code are declared as code records and each produces a memory-experiment source with detector and observable layouts, so a distance-d rotated patch is expressible and a code carrying both a Z-type and an X-type readout is expressible through Steane. A code record can now also be read into matrices rather than only into a circuit: css_code_matrices lifts its four blocks into a CssCodeMatrices record, which carries hz, hx, lz and lx together, so a code whose stabilizers are known reaches a code-capacity detector error model on either readout basis without a gadget being built for it and without losing a fault family. The families remain declared rather than constructed, and an arbitrary parity-check matrix still has no route in: a check states one ancilla and one CNOT direction fixed by its type, so a mixed X-and-Z stabilizer is refused, and a logical observable that is neither pure X nor pure Z is refused rather than half-read, so qLDPC, Reichardt and Floquet codes are absent and a colour code has no record even though the CSS shape now admits one. The code records themselves still expose no decode entry point, because decoding belongs to the decoder row and reads a detector error model rather than a code. The noise record is uniform scalars, so a per-location rate profile is not expressible either.
- `qec_decoder_family` (quantum_error_correction): Matching is now self-implemented rather than absent: the detector error model becomes a weighted decoding graph whose edge weight is log((1 - p) / p), and a syndrome is decoded exactly by enumerating the ways to pair its defective detectors and to route any of them to the graph's boundary. The row stays partial on scope, not on correctness. Matching needs a graphlike model and refuses a hyperedge rather than projecting it onto a pair, so a code whose mechanisms flip three or more detectors is outside this row's matching half. The pairing is enumerated, so a syndrome is bounded by a defect budget instead of decoded at scale. Belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding is absent, so the LDPC codes the baseline serves with it are not served here; the sliding-window decoder for a long-lived experiment is absent; and there is no decoder registry or plugin protocol, so a decoder is constructed directly rather than requested by name. The baseline's GPU decoders are deliberately not chased, because the CUDA-Q qLDPC decoder is a closed-source shared library, so only its interface position is a target and an Apache-2.0 implementation is the route if that scope is ever reached. The row fails closed on a second gap of its own: because the graph keeps one edge per mechanism, a model that states one detector-and-observable signature twice would become two parallel edges and the matcher would take the cheaper, so the decoder requires a unique signature before it weights anything and refuses a duplicate with the merge that resolves it named in the refusal. The cross-check half has landed and it is a comparison of two selections rather than an equality of two instruments: PyMatching is behind the `pymatching` extra and is never the authority, and because its own accumulator reports 3.9020747171643912 for a mechanism this row states as 3.9020746947749574 the graph it minimizes over is not exactly this one. The row therefore asserts the cheapest weight on every syndrome, the observables wherever the cheapest explanation is unique, and the two refusals as the same set, with a pinned tie on the distance-three repetition code so the tie clause is demonstrated. The remaining work inside this row is the registry, the two decoder families the matcher does not cover, and the hyperedge front end.
- `qec_stim_integration` (quantum_error_correction): All three halves now exist, and the row is partial on scope rather than on connection. Stim-backed sampling landed with the stabilizer engine, the detector error model half landed with the text reader and its own capability entry, and the join landed last: a memory circuit is lowered once, each configured noise location is placed at the instruction it belongs to, the result is executed on the stabilizer engine, and the detection events and observable flips are read off the recorded bits. A decoder built from that same circuit's model then decodes those events, so a logical-failure rate no longer needs the statevector ceiling that bounds construction. What the row still lacks is breadth of the noise grammar: a location is a data flip at a round boundary or a measurement flip at a check's readout, which is what the phenomenological record names, while a channel placed after an arbitrary gate has no location and is still declined. The x_ and z_ variants are absent for the same reason the code record is a Z-memory record. Decoding itself stays with the decoder row rather than being implied here. The row names three registry entries because the implementation genuinely spans three: the sampling half is `stabilizer_sampling`, the interchange half is `detector_error_model`, and the join that consumes both is `qec_memory_circuit_sampling`. The row is read only against cudaq-qec, which is where the detector error models live; where the two components divide this surface is recorded in `baseline.surface_ownership`.
- `third_party_target_sdk` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Absent, and it is the ecosystem entry point. Without it a provider can only be added by changing FlagQuantum.
- `provider_roster_breadth` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): FlagQuantum has fewer providers. The architectural requirement is a registration point a third party can use, which is why third_party_target_sdk is the higher-priority row.
- `simulator_plugin_admission` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): The decisive ecosystem gap. The extension protocol exists with an entry-point group, manifest, SDK version check, capability negotiation, and an ExecutionBackendExtension contract, and the runtime has a separate backend capability registry. The two never import each other, so an extension can be negotiated and discovered but cannot execute.
- `large_scale_statevector` (performance_and_scalability): The measured FlagQuantum point is a 32-qubit complex128 forward pass on one eight-accelerator node, which is a development-evidence result and is not comparable to the baseline scale. No row here is a performance claim.
- `production_sharded_statevector` (performance_and_scalability): The registered level is below production, so the sharded path cannot support a capacity-expansion claim yet.

**next** (33 open)

- `runtime_qubit_allocation` (language_and_programming_model): Wire count is fixed at circuit construction. Runtime allocation is designed in the QuantumIR level and is not implemented.
- `pauli_tracking_sbe` (language_and_programming_model): The sampling engine and the detector error model module both exist, so the condition this row was deferred on is met, and the row is now blocked on one narrower thing: the engine refuses a circuit carrying any noise instruction rather than tracking a Pauli frame through it. Pauli tracking is what would let a noisy Clifford circuit be sampled without a dense state.
- `global_seed_control` (language_and_programming_model): Seeding is per call rather than process wide. `ExecutionOptions` carries a seed and the training path carries its own seeder, so a user reproduces a run by threading a seed through each entry point instead of stating one seed for the session.
- `gate_decomposition_patterns` (compiler_and_ir): Native gate legalization exists but there is no rule library, so a target basis outside the legalization table cannot be reached.
- `basis_conversion` (compiler_and_ir): Partial coverage follows from the legalization table; there is no general conversion between two arbitrary named bases.
- `clifford_t_synthesis` (compiler_and_ir): Absent. The algorithms are published and vendor-neutral, and any implementation needs exact arithmetic that FlagQuantum does not currently carry.
- `angle_synthesis` (compiler_and_ir): Absent, and it shares the exact-arithmetic requirement with Clifford+T synthesis.
- `commutation_aware_rewrite` (compiler_and_ir): Absent. Needs the pass manager and an analysis-invalidation contract before a rewrite pass can be correct.
- `dead_code_elimination` (compiler_and_ir): Absent. Depends on the same pass infrastructure as commutation-aware rewriting.
- `target_text_emitters` (compiler_and_ir): An OpenQASM emitter exists. The emitter set is narrower than the CUDA-Q roster.
- `resource_estimation` (compiler_and_ir): Absent, and it cannot be made correct for loops and functions until ProgramIR exists, because a straight-line instruction list has no loop bound to estimate.
- `foreign_circuit_import` (compiler_and_ir): The Qiskit direction exists: an ecosystem adapter builds a FlagQuantum circuit from a provider object. OpenQASM import does not, and the OpenQASM surface FlagQuantum carries is an emitter, so a circuit that exists only as text cannot enter the framework.
- `backend_asynchronous_multi_qpu` (simulation_backends): Absent. FlagQuantum has single-target remote execution but no asynchronous fan-out across several QPUs with independent result streams.
- `backend_gpu_fabric` (simulation_backends): Absent as a FlagQuantum-owned transport. The replacement target is a FlagOS-family collective layer, not NCCL.
- `dynamics_schedule_and_integrators` (simulation_backends): The Lindblad engine integrates with one fixed-step RK4 over an explicitly declared time grid and a static Hamiltonian. There is no schedule object carrying time-dependent coefficients and no selectable integrator, so accuracy and stiffness cannot be traded per problem.
- `noise_model_callback` (noise_and_error_models): Per-gate (`NoiseModel.add(gate_names, channel)`) and per-qubit (`wires=`) static injection both exist, and lowering now refuses a rule that cannot apply. The callback form is absent, and `NoiseRule` carries a `KrausChannel` fixed at construction. A callback cannot be added to `NoiseRule` as it stands: `NoiseModel.identity` is a SHA-256 digest of `to_dict()`, and checkpoint resume and execution-plan identity both bind to it, so a channel chosen by an arbitrary callable would make identity unreproducible. Any such rule must be registered under a declared name and parameterization before it can participate in a model identity.
- `batched_trajectory` (noise_and_error_models): Trajectory simulation exists; batched execution across trajectories is narrower than the baseline.
- `unitary_mixture_degradation` (noise_and_error_models): Absent. The distinction matters because a unitary mixture admits sampling that a general channel does not.
- `noise_trajectory_shot_allocation` (noise_and_error_models): FlagQuantum samples Kraus trajectories, but the trajectory choice belongs to the engine rather than to the caller: the MPS trajectory path draws them implicitly and exposes an ensemble size, so there is no trajectory enumeration, no ordered or probabilistic selection strategy, and no shot-allocation policy. Those strategies are the whole of this row.
- `matrix_and_custom_operator` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): A stable operator schema and discovery interface exist, but there is no matrix-valued operator type that participates in the algebra.
- `exponential_pauli_operator` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Pauli words are representable. An explicit exponential-of-Pauli operator constructor is absent.
- `state_and_unitary_access` (algorithm_layer): Circuit.state exists. A full unitary accessor is absent.
- `algorithm_block_encoding_family` (algorithm_layer): The whole layer is absent. Qualtran is Apache-2.0 licensed and covers the same mathematics, so the plan is adaptation rather than research.
- `optimizer_library` (algorithm_layer): The gradient-based half is wider than the baseline's: the training path takes a PyTorch optimizer and the staged hybrid optimizer accepts adam, adamw, sgd, and LBFGS. The gradient-free half is the gap, because COBYLA, NelderMead, and SPSA have no implementation and the training entry point refuses an optimizer that is not a PyTorch one.
- `classical_data_encoding` (algorithm_layer): Absent as a public entry point. Amplitude encoding needs a normalized state-preparation path and angular encoding needs a feature-map constructor; the only related surface is a single data-reuploading helper in the simulation domain, reachable only as a module attribute.
- `qec_stim_user_migration` (quantum_error_correction): Absent, and its upstream counterpart is not where the surface list implies. cudaq-qec publishes no for-Stim-users page: the only page with that title in the CUDA-Q documentation belongs to the logical preview layer, and it states there that the layer does not simulate, sample, or decode, emits no detector annotations and no detector error models, and that those studies belong to the Stim ecosystem. So the document cannot be translated from that page, and reading the row's name as pointing at it would aim a `next`-priority capability at a component that produces no detector error model. The counterpart is cudaq-qec's own Stim surface: reading Stim detector error model text through dem_from_stim_text, sampling a model through dem_sampling, and decoding from a Stim DEM through the decoder framework. The document is conformance work rather than a new implementation, so it is still sequenced after the Stim integration row's halves are joined; until then a migration guide would describe a route that stops at the join.
- `logical_resource_estimation` (logical_and_ftqc_layer): Absent as a domain. Qualtran carries the same mathematics under an Apache-2.0 licence, so the planned route is adaptation into a FlagQuantum-owned report format aligned with capability-maturity.toml evidence.
- `runtime_endpoint` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Absent as a named contract. FlagQuantum has remote adapters and a deployment surface, but no provider-neutral endpoint object.
- `local_emulation` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Absent as a target-directed entry point. The noisy simulation it would build on exists.
- `realtime_feedback_loop` (realtime_control): Absent. This is the one capability that cannot be closed by software alone: it needs an FPGA and a remote-direct-memory-access capable network interface, so it requires a hardware partner.
- `realtime_transport` (realtime_control): Absent. The software side can define a vendor-neutral messaging protocol and device-call abstraction before hardware exists, and that is the part worth doing first.
- `realtime_host_api` (realtime_control): Absent. Defining the protocol is software work and is the prerequisite a hardware partner would implement against.
- `distribution_packaging` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): FlagQuantum ships a single package plus a development container. A metapackage that selects a FlagOS and accelerator generation has no equivalent and is needed for a domestic-accelerator install story.

**later** (20 open)

- `cpp_kernel_frontend` (language_and_programming_model): No C++ product surface exists. A domestic C++ front end would reuse the same LLVM/MLIR upstream as the Python path, so it is deferred rather than excluded.
- `qudit_and_photonic_operations` (language_and_programming_model): No qudit or photonic operation exists. Deferred as a distinct product line rather than a parity gap for the qubit runtime.
- `asynchronous_execution` (language_and_programming_model): Absent. Every FlagQuantum entry point returns a completed result, so there is no handle an outer loop could poll and no overlap between host work and a device run.
- `mlir_dialect_stack` (compiler_and_ir): FlagQuantum IR is a JSON instruction table. MLIR is Apache-2.0 licensed and vendor-neutral, so adopting it is a build decision rather than a dependency conflict. The internal levels come first.
- `backend_fermioniq_mps` (simulation_backends): Absent. It is an MPS variant with a narrower applicability than the maintained MPS path, so it follows rather than leads.
- `backend_photonics` (simulation_backends): Absent. Photonic simulation is a distinct product line and is deferred with the qudit operations it depends on.
- `boson_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Absent, and it has no consumer until a bosonic or photonic workload exists.
- `rydberg_analog_hamiltonian` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Absent. It is the observable-side input an analog neutral-atom target would need, so it follows that target rather than preceding it.
- `circuit_rendering_and_inspection` (algorithm_layer): Absent. The drawer renders a circuit to text or to a matplotlib figure and returns the text form, but there is no SVG string, no trace view, and no Bloch-sphere picture. `draw` itself is counted in the execution entry points row rather than here.
- `qec_dialect` (quantum_error_correction): Absent, and deliberately sequenced after the internal levels stabilize. A second dialect before the first one exists would be a parallel scaffold.
- `qec_logical_operations` (quantum_error_correction): Absent. It belongs to the logical layer below and shares the Qualtran adaptation plan. The baseline exposes this as the ~70-name `logical.*` preview namespace measured from a live CUDA-Q 0.16.0 install, which also carries the patch, gadget, protocol, and program records the operations compose; the semantic core (lattice surgery, product rotation, distillation) is what this row tracks, and the surrounding records are why the row is a layer rather than a function.
- `qec_transport_and_objectives` (quantum_error_correction): Absent. These are hardware-shaped QEC models that need the corresponding target to be meaningful.
- `arithmetic_bloqs` (logical_and_ftqc_layer): Absent, and it is reachable through the same Qualtran adaptation as logical resource estimation.
- `physical_placement_and_scheduling` (logical_and_ftqc_layer): Absent. It also depends on a physical target model, so it follows the compiler routing work.
- `ftqc_device_modeling` (logical_and_ftqc_layer): Absent. It is a modeling surface with no consumer until logical resource estimation exists.
- `logical_gadget_verification` (logical_and_ftqc_layer): Absent, and it depends on both the logical layer and the QEC decoders.
- `realtime_sensor_bridge` (realtime_control): Absent and NVIDIA-specific. A FlagOS-family equivalent is the replacement target, and it follows the protocol definition.
- `stable_c_abi` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): Absent by decision rather than by omission. A stable C ABI requires a real performance backend as its justification, so it is sequenced after the Python admission path proves the boundary by replacement.
- `cpp_api_surface` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): Absent. It is not a product goal for the Python-first FlagQuantum surface, and it is listed here so the gap is recorded rather than implied.
- `vendor_certification` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): Absent. FlagQuantum evidence governance is stronger than the baseline in maturity levels and benchmark auditing, but there is no certification path by which a vendor attests to a backend.

| `python_ast_kernel` | @cudaq.kernel decorator compiling a Python function body through an AST bridge | partial | now | none | none | FlagQuantum builds circuits through an explicit builder API. There is no AST layer, so a user cannot write a Python function body as a kernel. |

| `type_system_qubit_register_view` | qubit, qvector, and qview types with linearity rules | unsupported | now | none | `ir` | CircuitIR 1.0 addresses wires by integer index and has no type system. The designed QuantumIR type system and its reference-versus-value linearity rules are not implemented. |

| `custom_operation_registration` | register_operation for user-defined operations with backend capability negotiation | partial | now | none | none | Circuit.any accepts a raw unitary but there is no operation registry, no schema, and no backend degradation contract for a user-defined operation. |

| `pauli_tracking_sbe` | Pauli tracking stabilizer-basis expansion for noisy simulation | unsupported | next | none | none | The sampling engine and the detector error model module both exist, so the condition this row was deferred on is met, and the row is now blocked on one narrower thing: the engine refuses a circuit carrying any noise instruction rather than tracking a Pauli frame through it. Pauli tracking is what would let a noisy Clifford circuit be sampled without a dense state. |
| `asynchronous_execution` | run_async, sample_async, observe_async, and evolve_async with their result handles | unsupported | later | none | none | Absent. Every FlagQuantum entry point returns a completed result, so there is no handle an outer loop could poll and no overlap between host work and a device run. |
| `global_seed_control` | set_random_seed for a process-wide sampling and noise seed | partial | next | none | none | Seeding is per call rather than process wide. `ExecutionOptions` carries a seed and the training path carries its own seeder, so a user reproduces a run by threading a seed through each entry point instead of stating one seed for the session. |

#### Noise and error models

Domain id: `noise_and_error_models`

| `kraus_channel_algebra` | Kraus channels and general noise channels | partial | now | none | `noisy_simulation` | A general Kraus constructor exists and is validated. `KrausChannel` accepts an arbitrary operator list, refuses a set that is not trace-preserving (completeness compared at `atol = rtol = 1e-6`) and a dimension that is not a positive power of two, serializes through the `flagquantum.kraus_channel.v1` schema, and reaches simulation through `NoiseModel.add` and `Circuit.noisy_density_matrix`. What is absent is the operator type the CUDA-Q surface builds a channel from: no matrix-valued operator participates in operator algebra, which is the gap `matrix_and_custom_operator` already records. |
| `noise_model_callback` | Noise model callbacks injecting noise by operation type at runtime | partial | next | none | `noisy_simulation` | Per-gate (`NoiseModel.add(gate_names, channel)`) and per-qubit (`wires=`) static injection both exist, and lowering now refuses a rule that cannot apply. The callback form is absent, and `NoiseRule` carries a `KrausChannel` fixed at construction. A callback cannot be added to `NoiseRule` as it stands: `NoiseModel.identity` is a SHA-256 digest of `to_dict()`, and checkpoint resume and execution-plan identity both bind to it, so a channel chosen by an arbitrary callable would make identity unreproducible. Any such rule must be registered under a declared name and parameterization before it can participate in a model identity. |

The row stays partial because conversion is narrower than the baseline at the input end: `from_memory_circuit` accepts one circuit record and one noise record, so an arbitrary circuit carrying detector and observable annotations has no route to a model, and a non-Pauli channel is refused rather than decomposed. `flagquantum/qec/IMPLEMENTATION.md` records the sweeps and the arithmetic. |

Qualtran is Apache-2.0 licensed and covers the same mathematics, so the plan is adaptation rather than research. |
| `error_mitigation` | Zero-noise extrapolation, probabilistic error cancellation, and Clifford data regression | partial | now | none | `algorithms_zero_noise_extrapolation` | Zero-noise extrapolation only. An observable is measured at several error strengths by scaling the one error-probability parameter each noise channel declares, and the curve is continued to zero by polynomial least squares or Richardson extrapolation, which reports the residual it left and the variance amplification of its weights. The channel families whose parameters are not error probabilities are refused by name, and a model that declares a readout rule is refused rather than measured without it, because the estimate is Tr(O rho) and classical readout confusion is applied after measurement. Probabilistic error cancellation and Clifford data regression are absent, and so is readout-error mitigation. |
| `variational_algorithms` | VQE and QAOA solver libraries | partial | now | none | `algorithms_grover_search` | VQE-class and several algorithm primitives exist as separate registered capabilities rather than a solver family, so the surface shape differs from the baseline. |
| `differentiable_training` | No equivalent; CUDA-Q has no reverse-mode differentiation through simulation | supported | now | none | `sharded_statevector_training` | FlagQuantum advantage, not parity. Reverse-mode autograd through simulation, the Module and train lifecycle, and gradient preservation under sharding are capabilities the CUDA-Q baseline does not offer. <br><br>Narrower scope at this status: The registered level covers the local training path. Gradient correctness under sharding is registered separately and is not asserted here. |
| `optimizer_library` | cudaq.optimizers with Adam, COBYLA, GradientDescent, LBFGS, NelderMead, SGD, and SPSA | partial | next | none | none | The gradient-based half is wider than the baseline's: the training path takes a PyTorch optimizer and the staged hybrid optimizer accepts adam, adamw, sgd, and LBFGS. The gradient-free half is the gap, because COBYLA, NelderMead, and SPSA have no implementation and the training entry point refuses an optimizer that is not a PyTorch one. |
| `classical_data_encoding` | amplitude_encode and angular_encode mapping classical features onto a state | unsupported | next | none | none | Absent as a public entry point. Amplitude encoding needs a normalized state-preparation path and angular encoding needs a feature-map constructor; the only related surface is a single data-reuploading helper in the simulation domain, reachable only as a module attribute. |
| `circuit_rendering_and_inspection` | getSVGstring, display, display_trace, and add_to_bloch_sphere over a drawing surface that also returns text | unsupported | later | none | none | Absent. The drawer renders a circuit to text or to a matplotlib figure and returns the text form, but there is no SVG string, no trace view, and no Bloch-sphere picture. `draw` itself is counted in the execution entry points row rather than here. |

#### Quantum error correction

Domain id: `quantum_error_correction`

CUDA-Q surface: cudaq-qec library, detector, detectors, and logical_observable annotations in a kernel, dem, dem_from_kernel, and DEMResult, extract_syndrome, circuit-to-DEM round trip, Stim integration, the logical.* preview namespace, QEC MLIR dialect, GPU decoders, surface, Steane, and qLDPC codes, lattice surgery and magic state distillation, transport, rounds, objectives, neutral atoms, for-stim-users migration

| Capability | CUDA-Q baseline | Status | Priority | Dependency class | FlagQuantum maturity | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qec_code_library` | cudaq-qec codes expressed as kernels, with numerical experiment APIs | partial | now | none | `stabilizer_code_memory_circuit` | The repetition code, the rotated surface code and the Steane code are declared as code records and each produces a memory-experiment source with detector and observable layouts, so a distance-d rotated patch is expressible and a code carrying both a Z-type and an X-type readout is expressible through Steane. A code record can now also be read into matrices rather than only into a circuit: css_code_matrices lifts its four blocks into a CssCodeMatrices record, which carries hz, hx, lz and lx together, so a code whose stabilizers are known reaches a code-capacity detector error model on either readout basis without a gadget being built for it and without losing a fault family. The families remain declared rather than constructed, and an arbitrary parity-check matrix still has no route in: a check states one ancilla and one CNOT direction fixed by its type, so a mixed X-and-Z stabilizer is refused, and a logical observable that is neither pure X nor pure Z is refused rather than half-read, so qLDPC, Reichardt and Floquet codes are absent and a colour code has no record even though the CSS shape now admits one. The code records themselves still expose no decode entry point, because decoding belongs to the decoder row and reads a detector error model rather than a code. The noise record is uniform scalars, so a per-location rate profile is not expressible either. |
| `qec_decoder_family` | Minimum-weight perfect matching, belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding, and sliding-window decoders | partial | now | B_open_neutral | `detector_error_matching_decoder` | Matching is now self-implemented rather than absent: the detector error model becomes a weighted decoding graph whose edge weight is log((1 - p) / p), and a syndrome is decoded exactly by enumerating the ways to pair its defective detectors and to route any of them to the graph's boundary. The row stays partial on scope, not on correctness. Matching needs a graphlike model and refuses a hyperedge rather than projecting it onto a pair, so a code whose mechanisms flip three or more detectors is outside this row's matching half. The pairing is enumerated, so a syndrome is bounded by a defect budget instead of decoded at scale. Belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding is absent, so the LDPC codes the baseline serves with it are not served here; the sliding-window decoder for a long-lived experiment is absent; and there is no decoder registry or plugin protocol, so a decoder is constructed directly rather than requested by name. The baseline's GPU decoders are deliberately not chased, because the CUDA-Q qLDPC decoder is a closed-source shared library, so only its interface position is a target and an Apache-2.0 implementation is the route if that scope is ever reached. The row fails closed on a second gap of its own: because the graph keeps one edge per mechanism, a model that states one detector-and-observable signature twice would become two parallel edges and the matcher would take the cheaper, so the decoder requires a unique signature before it weights anything and refuses a duplicate with the merge that resolves it named in the refusal. The cross-check half has landed and it is a comparison of two selections rather than an equality of two instruments: PyMatching is behind the `pymatching` extra and is never the authority, and because its own accumulator reports 3.9020747171643912 for a mechanism this row states as 3.9020746947749574 the graph it minimizes over is not exactly this one. The row therefore asserts the cheapest weight on every syndrome, the observables wherever the cheapest explanation is unique, and the two refusals as the same set, with a pinned tie on the distance-three repetition code so the tie clause is demonstrated. The remaining work inside this row is the registry, the two decoder families the matcher does not cover, and the hyperedge front end. |
| `qec_stim_integration` | Stim sampling and detector error model interoperability | partial | now | B_open_neutral | `stabilizer_sampling`, `detector_error_model`, `qec_memory_circuit_sampling` | All three halves now exist, and the row is partial on scope rather than on connection. Stim-backed sampling landed with the stabilizer engine, the detector error model half landed with the text reader and its own capability entry, and the join landed last: a memory circuit is lowered once, each configured noise location is placed at the instruction it belongs to, the result is executed on the stabilizer engine, and the detection events and observable flips are read off the recorded bits. A decoder built from that same circuit's model then decodes those events, so a logical-failure rate no longer needs the statevector ceiling that bounds construction. What the row still lacks is breadth of the noise grammar: a location is a data flip at a round boundary or a measurement flip at a check's readout, which is what the phenomenological record names, while a channel placed after an arbitrary gate has no location and is still declined. The x_ and z_ variants are absent for the same reason the code record is a Z-memory record. Decoding itself stays with the decoder row rather than being implied here. The row names three registry entries because the implementation genuinely spans three: the sampling half is `stabilizer_sampling`, the interchange half is `detector_error_model`, and the join that consumes both is `qec_memory_circuit_sampling`. The row is read only against cudaq-qec, which is where the detector error models live; where the two components divide this surface is recorded in `baseline.surface_ownership`. <br><br>Narrower scope at this status: No sampling of error-corrected logical operations, and no noise grammar wider than the phenomenological record. A channel placed after a named gate, an x_ or z_ variant over a state preparation, and pymatching- or stim-driven logical-error-rate estimation all remain absent, so a circuit whose noise is neither a round-boundary data flip nor a readout flip is declined rather than sampled. |
| `qec_dialect` | A QEC MLIR dialect | unsupported | later | B_open_neutral | `ir` | Absent, and deliberately sequenced after the internal levels stabilize. A second dialect before the first one exists would be a parallel scaffold. |
| `qec_logical_operations` | Lattice surgery, product rotation, and magic state distillation | unsupported | later | B_open_neutral | none | Absent. It belongs to the logical layer below and shares the Qualtran adaptation plan. The baseline exposes this as the ~70-name `logical.*` preview namespace measured from a live CUDA-Q 0.16.0 install, which also carries the patch, gadget, protocol, and program records the operations compose; the semantic core (lattice surgery, product rotation, distillation) is what this row tracks, and the surrounding records are why the row is a layer rather than a function. |
| `qec_transport_and_objectives` | Transport, rounds, objectives, ccz, and neutral-atom QEC models | unsupported | later | none | none | Absent. These are hardware-shaped QEC models that need the corresponding target to be meaningful. |
| `qec_stim_user_migration` | A documented migration path for Stim users | unsupported | next | none | `detector_error_model` | Absent, and its upstream counterpart is not where the surface list implies. cudaq-qec publishes no for-Stim-users page: the only page with that title in the CUDA-Q documentation belongs to the logical preview layer, and it states there that the layer does not simulate, sample, or decode, emits no detector annotations and no detector error models, and that those studies belong to the Stim ecosystem. So the document cannot be translated from that page, and reading the row's name as pointing at it would aim a `next`-priority capability at a component that produces no detector error model. The counterpart is cudaq-qec's own Stim surface: reading Stim detector error model text through dem_from_stim_text, sampling a model through dem_sampling, and decoding from a Stim DEM through the decoder framework. The document is conformance work rather than a new implementation, so it is still sequenced after the Stim integration row's halves are joined; until then a migration guide would describe a route that stops at the join. |
